blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — newborn assessment and interpretation of Apgar findings
stem: A nurse is calculating a 1-minute Apgar score for a newborn whose body is pink but whose hands and feet remain blue. How many points should be assigned for the color component?
rationale: Current StatPearls/NCBI guidance states that each Apgar component is scored 0, 1, or 2. For color, a pale or blue newborn receives 0 points, a newborn who is pink with blue extremities receives 1 point, and an entirely pink newborn receives 2 points. Therefore B is correct. A corresponds to generalized pallor or cyanosis, C requires the newborn to be entirely pink, and D is incorrect because color is one of the five scored Apgar components.
educational_objective: Assign 1 Apgar color point when a newborn is pink centrally with persistent blue extremities (acrocyanosis).
source_organization: StatPearls / NCBI Bookshelf, National Library of Medicine
source_version_date: Last Update January 31, 2026; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Technique or Treatment > Color: pale or blue = 0; pink with blue extremities = 1; entirely pink = 2; each Apgar category is assigned 0, 1, or 2.
source_claim_supported: A newborn who is pink centrally but has blue extremities receives 1 point for the Apgar color component.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: perform focused assessments; recognize trends and changes in client condition; monitor diagnostic/assessment findings and intervene as needed.
correction_summary: Standardized option capitalization and retained the exact 0/1/2 Apgar color scoring construct; difficulty metadata was corrected to easy because this is direct application of one scoring criterion.

audit_findings.stem: PASS — provides the exact color finding needed and asks only for the color component, avoiding dependence on other Apgar elements.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — 0 points applies to generalized pallor or blue coloration.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS — pink body with blue extremities is exactly the 1-point criterion.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — 2 points requires the neonate to be entirely pink.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — color is explicitly one of the five scored Apgar components.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — B uniquely matches the source-defined finding.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — no other score fits central pink coloration with blue extremities.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — option capitalization is standardized and the numeric alternatives are parallel.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — immediate newborn assessment and interpretation of findings align with Reduction of Risk Potential.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether acrocyanosis could be considered normal and therefore score 2. StatPearls explicitly assigns pink with blue extremities 1 point despite common peripheral cyanosis, so B remains uniquely correct.
